To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamics of the visual cortex is crucial for the representation of visual information in a free-viewing scenario.

the optimal coding strategy of the V1 network is to adapt the strength of the recurrent excitation to the time elapsed since the beginning of the fixation period, and that the adaptation is driven by the intrinsic property of spike-frequency adaption of pyramidal neurons.

(1) spike-frequency adaptation is a mechanism for dynamic cortical processing; (2) the dynamics of cortical activity are a consequence of the interplay between feed-forward and recurrent processing; (3) the dynamics of recurrent processing are a consequence of spike-frequency adaptation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) What are the properties of a neural code that allows for a reliable representation of the visual scene?
the dynamic coding of visual information in V1 and the role of spike-frequency adaptation for the optimal representation of stimuli.
the question of what kind of information processing strategy is optimal for the representation of visual information in the primary visual cortex (V1) of primates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal coding strategy for a noisy representation of visual stimuli in primary visual cortex is to dynamically adjust the strength of recurrent inhibition with time, which can be achieved via the instrinsic mechanism of spike-frequency adaptation.
spike-frequency adaptation is a necessary mechanism in order to achieve a dynamic coding strategy in V1, which in turn is a prerequisite for the representation of visual information over time.
spike-frequency adaptation in the primary visual cortex serves as a mechanism for the dynamic representation of visual stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dynamic coding scheme is optimal for the neural system in order to represent visual stimuli.

the dynamic coding in V-1 is mediated by the intrinsic property of spike-frequency adapation of cortical neurons, and the optimal representation of the stimulus is archived by a dynamic competition between orientation selective neurons.
the optimal coding strategy for V1 in a saccadic scenario is to have a strong initial competition between neurons, followed by a gradual attenuation with time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spike-frequency adaptation of cortical pyramidal cells may be an intrinsic mechanism for dynamic coding, i.e. the representation of a visual stimulus in a time-dependent fashion.

the dynamics of adaptation is a key mechanism to achieve a dynamic coding of visual stimuli in V1, and that it is a mechanism that is independent of the specific details of the visual stimulus and the visual system under consideration.
spike-frequency adaptation is a key mechanism in the brain for dynamic coding of visual stimuli.
